segments.t: Since the restaurant has no sommelier on duty, bartender Kostya puts on an apron and tries to sell a guest the most expensive bottle of wine on the menu to pair with lamb. When the guest exposes Kostya's complete lack of wine knowledge, Nastya suggests paying for professional sommelier lessons.

'Allow me to offer you a wonderful wine with your lamb.' Explaining that the guest should allow him to offer the guest a wonderful wine with the guest's lamb lays the cards on the table for the guest. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.

'Why are you offering me the most expensive wine?' Asking why Kostya offering him the most expensive wine is is how the guest puts Kostya on the spot.

'Because expensive wine is always the very best!' Once because expensive wine is always the very best, Kostya makes sure the guest hears every word. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.

'Expensive wine does not mean the very best at all.' Admitting that expensive wine does not mean the very best at all shows the guest being honest for a change.

'Let tasty wine dominate on your table!' Letting tasty wine dominate on the guest's table shows Kostya is done holding back. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.

'I asked to call a sommelier, not a bartender!' The guest declares that he asked to call a sommelier not a bartender as the tension in the room peaks. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.

'Excuse me, choose any good wine on my tab!' Here choosing any good wine on his tab lets Kostya's real feelings break through. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.

'Kostik, let's sign you up for sommelier courses!' Once someone let them sign the guest up for sommelier courses, Nastya makes sure the guest hears every word. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
